claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys occupy a vast compositional space.
Structure–property relationships across the refractory-HEA compositional space are largely unexplored.
Efficient high-throughput tools are needed to rapidly explore the vast HEA compositional space.
Historical experimental results and simulation data can be integrated to train a machine-learning model for screening refractory-HEA compositions.
A machine-learning high-throughput screening tool will rapidly identify refractory-HEA compositions with an optimal balance of intrinsic strength, ductility, and low density.
High-quality, diverse training data should span multiple elements and processing parameters.
The model can predict lattice distortion and phase distribution.
Predicted lattice distortion and phase distribution correlate with improved mechanical properties.
The machine-learning model can detect correlations among composition, processing conditions, and resulting microstructure by analyzing large datasets.
Detected composition–processing–microstructure correlations enable prediction of compositions with enhanced strength and ductility.
Detected correlations enable prediction of refractory-HEA compositions with reduced density.
Machine-learning-selected compositions will have superior intrinsic mechanical properties and lower weight than compositions identified using traditional thermo-kinetic simulation methods.
Machine-learning screening will reduce screening time and computational cost relative to traditional simulation-based methods.
CALPHAD can perform high-throughput calculations over multicomponent alloy composition spaces.
CALPHAD calculations require computational software and a thermodynamic database.
Traditional thermo-kinetic and ab initio methods require extensive computational resources and experimental iterations.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning approach depends on the availability and quality of integrated experimental and simulation data.
Predictive power may diminish in sparsely sampled, incomplete, or biased compositional regions.
Experimental validation is required to determine the improvement in screening speed and property-prediction accuracy.
Failure of a majority of machine-learning-selected alloys to show statistically significant improvements under identical processing conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
